decisions.quote:
In a previous study, deception was accurately detected
in at least 90% of the participants in two independent cohorts. This study attempted to replicate those findings using a
different scanner and location.
Methods: Healthy participants 18-50 years of age were recruited from the local community. After providing written
informed consent, participants were screened to ensure that they were healthy, not taking any medications, and safe to
have an MRI. For the testing paradigm, subjects chose one of two objects (ring or watch) to “steal” and placed it in their
locker. Participants were then scanned while being visually presented with a series of questions. Functional MRI analysis
was performed in the same manner as described in Kozel et al. 2005. A Chi-Squared test was used to test for a significant
difference between the results in the previous study and in this replication study.
decisions.reason: The paper explicitly re-tests the ring-watch fMRI deception detection protocol, individual diagnostic accuracy (93% in the n=30 Model Building Group and 90% in the n=31 Model Testing Group), and Lie-minus-True group activation map from Reference [5]: Kozel, F. A., Johnson, K. A., Mu, Q., Grenesko, E. L., Laken, S. J., & George, M. S. (2005), 'Detecting deception using functional magnetic resonance imaging,' Biol. Psychiatry, 58(8), 605-613. Resolving the competing_supported_matches flag, shipped row 660 matches blind target_index 2 (Ref [5]), which is also the direct target closest in the replication chain ahead of earlier group-level studies in Refs [3] and [4].

decisions.quote:
This method for detecting deception was successfully
replicated on a different scanner at a different location for
both the individual and group analyses. This suggests that
our deception detection methodology is neither scanner nor
location dependent.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree on 'successful'. For Kozel et al. (2005), individual deception was accurately detected in 25/29 (86%) participants, with no statistically significant difference from the 28/31 (90%) blind testing cohort in Kozel et al. (2005) (Chi-Squared = 0.246, p = 0.6197), and the Lie-minus-True group map replicated significant activation in the right orbitofrontal, right inferior frontal, right middle frontal, and right cingulate gyrus regions. Although the left middle temporal gyrus was not significantly active in the group map (and was not part of the individual detection model), the authors state an explicit overall verdict that the method was 'successfully replicated on a different scanner at a different location for both the individual and group analyses', which governs under Codebook Step 3 Rule 1. Lower accuracy mentioned in the Discussion for Reference [30] concerns a separate mock-sabotage study rather than this paper's replication.

decisions.quote:
After successfully replicating the group results of fMRI
detection of deception in a laboratory paradigm involving
subjects giving deceptive and truthful answers [3, 4], we
developed a method to identify deception at the individual
level [5].
decisions.reason: Under the Codebook Step 2 replication-chain rule ('when the finding has already been re-tested by others, the target is the study closest to this paper in the chain — the one it actually re-tests — not the chain's original source') and consistent with the prior Argon adjudication (27dd47e58906b908bd5d7e819d1bcc262bbffaed7af4d2c61baf63107bc2bbfd.json; prior state file 5a996c5b...json is absent), Reference [3] (Kozel et al., 2004, J. Neuropsychiatr. Clin. Neurosci., 16(3), 295-305; blind target_index 0) is the original 2004 group-level pilot study at the start of a four-study replication chain ([3] -> [4] -> [5] -> current 2009 study). The study closest in the chain whose ring/watch mock-crime protocol, individual ROI detection model, and Lie-minus-True group activation map (compared directly against the Kozel et al. 2005 Model Building Group in Figure 1) are actually re-tested by this paper is Reference [5] (Kozel et al., 2005, Biol. Psychiatry, 58(8), 605-613, DOI 10.1016/j.biopsych.2005.07.040), which is already represented by retained shipped row input_row_index '660' (blind target_index 2). Note also that Luna's triage omission_quote failed mechanical validation because it spliced out parenthetical statistical thresholds from lines 195-198.
